vulnerabilities.description: PARTIALLY FIXED — the previous MEDIUM is closed for DIRECT targets and still open for INDIRECT dependents, and the two layers now contradict each other. packages/mcp-server/src/eap/recall-projection.ts:57 `if (!directTargets.has(claimId)) continue` projects only the contestation's own targetClaimIds, but graph-core/src/eap/recall.ts:204 assigns EVERY claim in the reverse closure `normativelyResolvedState = 'recalled'`, and that value is durably written into recall_cases.state and into the scar. Reproduced end-to-end on 511a61d: candidates k1 and k2 advanced to 'admitted' in horizon h1 (child of root); committed claims k1 and k2 seeded with k2.refs = ['k1']; cognitive.contest(k1, invalidating) -> admitted; cognitive.recall returned affectedClaimIds ['k1','k2'] with degradedClaims listing BOTH as previousState 'admitted' -> newState 'recalled'. Afterwards `SELECT candidate_id,state FROM candidates` returned k1='recalled' (correct, the fix works) and k2='admitted'. cognitive.propose CONCRETIZE on k2 -> ok:true (seq 5), VERIFY -> ok:true (seq 6), and cognitive.promote k2 from h1 into root -> ok:true, minting proposal prop-prom-h1-root-... and entering k2 into the parent horizon. So a claim the domain itself recorded as recalled, resting on a premise that was retracted, completed its lifecycle and was promoted into a parent horizon. Test-scenarios 1.1 'Should preserve the historical scar when Recall completes' ("a Recall Case that has degraded its normatively resolved affected claims") is satisfied durably but not on the read model. HELD AT MEDIUM, NOT HIGH, DELIBERATELY: 003 §Explicitly Deferred Decisions defers "the exact destination status of indirect recall dependents", so the projection is right to refuse to invent one, and the graph-level consequence DOES land — both cells (auth:L1 and billing:L1) were correctly written to 'suspended' with last_flip_by 'recall:recall-contest_1', verified in a separate reproduction over committed claims. What is missing is not a destination status but any gate at all: promotion and VERIFY should refuse a candidate that sits inside a completed recall closure, whatever status the ADR eventually assigns it. This likely needs the ADR amendment 003 requires rather than a unilateral code decision.

NEW. The advertised MCP inputSchemas in packages/mcp-server/src/transport.ts:170-193 omit fields the handlers require, so a client driven purely by tools/list cannot perform a lifecycle transition or a promotion at all. Reproduced against tools/list on 511a61d: cognitive.propose advertises properties [token, horizonId, candidateId, command] and required [token, horizonId, candidateId, command] — `evidence` is neither advertised nor required, yet tools/eap.ts:216 refuses EVIDENCE_REQUIRED without it; calling with exactly the advertised contract returned {ok:false, EVIDENCE_REQUIRED}. cognitive.promote advertises [token, childHorizonId, targetParentHorizonId] with no `candidateIds`, yet tools/eap.ts:424 now refuses MALFORMED_CONTRACT 'Promotion requires at least one candidate to distil'; calling with exactly the advertised contract returned {ok:false, MALFORMED_CONTRACT}. `basedOnSeq` — the whole optimistic-concurrency contract that retry #6 hardened — is advertised on no tool at all, and cognitive.recall advertises neither `checkpoint` nor `batchSize` although both are validated by the handler. The schemas are permissive (no additionalProperties:false), so packages/client works and the suite stays green; the defect is that the only machine-readable description of the reachable surface is wrong. For an MCP server whose consumer is an agent reading that schema, this is the interface. Test-scenarios 3.3 'oversized or out-of-range contract values' is now enforced for a parameter clients are never told exists.

An Operator Approval is bound to a scope but not to a capability, and the scope is a string the REQUESTER declares. Reproduced: registered approval 'ap-del' scope 'delete:tenant-a/docs' basedOnSeq 5 against a tenant whose observed sequence is 5, then called gateway.execute with capabilityId 'infra.wipe_everything' and contract {targetScope:'delete:tenant-a/docs', payload:{path:'/'}} — status COMPLETED, provider invoked, the irreversible effect ran. Nothing in CapabilityGateway or authorizeCapability relates targetScope to capabilityId or to the payload; classificationMap maps capabilityId only to reversible/irreversible. Rated LOW and reported for completeness rather than as an implementation defect: 004 §1.2 binds an approval to "an approver, scope, expiry, provenance, and basedOnSeq" and the implementation enforces exactly that, correctly and fail-closed (an unregistered id is APPROVAL_MISSING, an unparseable expiry is APPROVAL_EXPIRED, a spent id cannot be re-armed, and the sequence operand is now the host's). Confining a grant to the capability it was issued for is a spec decision, not a fix the developer should make unilaterally.

Unchanged and openly deferred: the Horizon Budget Ledger is stored and never enforced. tools/eap.ts:148 writes budget_allocated on eapInitiate; nothing increments budget_consumed or compares the two; HorizonStore.saveTransition's budgetConsumed override has no caller; the BudgetLedger / HorizonBudgetExhausted logic in graph-core/src/eap/horizon.ts is wired to nothing reachable. Test-scenarios 1.1 'Should escalate without promotion when the Horizon budget is exhausted' has no implementation. Re-confirmed on 511a61d.

NEW, low reach. tools/eap.ts:267 `const expected = nextStateMap[currentCandState] ?? { command: 'DELIBERATE', next: 'deliberated' }` means ANY candidates.state value outside the six-member CandidateState union is silently treated as the START of the lifecycle. Reproduced: UPDATE candidates SET state='weird-state', then cognitive.propose DELIBERATE returned ok:true and rewrote the row to 'deliberated'. Adding 'recalled' to the map (the correct fix for the recall case) closed the one reachable instance, but the fallback itself is still a fail-open default on a lifecycle gate: an unrecognized state should be a typed refusal, not a reset to 'proposed'. Only reachable through direct column corruption or a rebuildFromJsonl replay of a mirror written by a future/foreign schema version, hence LOW.

edgeCasesMissed: RE-VERIFIED CLOSED BY REPRODUCTION, recorded for the log. (1) AUTH_BYPASS on caller-supplied currentSeq is CLOSED: CapabilityGateway now takes a required ObservedSequenceSource and overwrites request.currentSeq at capability-gateway.ts:150. The exact prior exploit — approval 'apS' bound to basedOnSeq 99, tenant whose real MAX(seq) over horizons is 0, execute with currentSeq:99 — returned REFUSED APPROVAL_STALE_SEQ 'Approval based on sequence 99 but current sequence is 0' with 0 provider invocations. The constructor throws when the source is absent, so no construction site can silently reinstate it. (2) Recall degradation now reaches the knowledge tables for direct targets: after recall, candidates.k1 = 'recalled', CONCRETIZE is refused ILLEGAL_TRANSITION 'recalled knowledge has no lifecycle successor', and re-contesting k1 is refused RESOURCE_ABSENT because it no longer resolves as admitted knowledge. Truth-ownership suspension lands too: cells auth:L1 and billing:L1 went to 'suspended' with last_flip_by 'recall:<caseId>', and the claims table was correctly NOT rewritten (004 §1.1). (3) basedOnSeq is CLOSED: 1e308 -> MALFORMED_CONTRACT 'no greater than 9007199254740991'; a future base 9999 against horizon seq 0 -> STALE_BASE; equality is enforced in both propose and promote. (4) eapPromote is CLOSED and idempotent: a second identical promote returned the SAME promotionId with replayed:true, the child horizon seq stayed at 5 across both calls, and exactly one proposals row exists; two CONCURRENT promotes over one candidate set also produced one proposal and one sequence burn. (5) parseStored is CLOSED: corrupting contestations.target_claim_ids to '{not json' and calling cognitive.recall returned a typed {ok:false, RESOURCE_ABSENT, 'Stored contestations.target_claim_ids ... is not readable JSON'} instead of a SyntaxError. (6) eapContest evidence is CLOSED: [{a:1},'ok-ev'] -> EVIDENCE_REQUIRED, whole contract refused, nothing stored. (7) The in-process recall race is CLOSED: three concurrent cognitive.recall calls for one contestationId produced ONE recall_cases row, one burned recalls sequence, one winner and two replayed:true responses. (8) Tenant isolation holds: recalling in tenant ta left tenant tb's identically-named candidate at 'admitted', and tb recalling ta's contestation id was refused RECALL_UNPROVEN 'not found'.

PRIMARY REMAINING GAP (see the MEDIUM DATA_INTEGRITY entry): an indirect dependent inside a completed recall closure is degraded to 'recalled' in the durable case and the scar, but keeps its 'admitted' row in `candidates`, then climbs CONCRETIZE and VERIFY and is promoted into the parent horizon. 003 defers the destination status; it does not defer the existence of a gate. The minimum honest fix is for eapPromote and the VERIFY transition to refuse a candidate that appears in any completed recall closure, deferring only what its final status should be.

Test-scenarios 1.1 Horizon 'Should retain horizon-local authority when assignment to another Horizon is attempted': still no code path refuses an explicit cross-horizon Relative Authority assignment. Promotion correctly enters every candidate at 'proposed' in the parent (re-verified: k2 promoted into root landed at 'proposed', authority is not inherited), so the invariant holds by construction — but the explicit refusal the scenario asks for does not exist.

Approval freshness is a MONOTONE GLOBAL MAX(seq) over the tenant's horizons (eap-repositories.ts:446), and any caller can drive it upward at will with cognitive.propose. An approval bound to a FUTURE sequence is therefore refused only until the tenant's activity reaches that number, at which point it becomes spendable against a world state the operator never saw — reproduced: the same 'apS' grant that was refused at seq 0 executed COMPLETED after setObservedSeq(99). Not scored as a defect: the spec's rule is basedOnSeq === currentSeq and that is exactly what is enforced, and the normal case (a grant bound to the CURRENT sequence) is invalidated by any subsequent activity, which is the fail-closed direction. Worth an ADR note on whether an approval should also carry a horizon binding.

Advertised-schema divergence (see the MEDIUM MALFORMED_CONTRACT entry) also means test-scenarios 3.3 boundary coverage is unreachable for a schema-driven client: it cannot send basedOnSeq at all, so the STALE_BASE and MAX_SEQUENCE gates retry #6 built are exercised only by the in-repo client and the test suite.

Still knowingly deferred and re-confirmed present, not re-scored beyond the LOW budget entry: promotion_events pagination/retention (SqlitePromotionRepository.getEvents has no LIMIT/OFFSET over an unbounded append-only table); cross-process / cross-connection concurrency (every concurrency test still shares one bun:sqlite handle, so SQLITE_BUSY on the reserve/consume path is untested — the in-process races are now genuinely closed); packages/client/src/eap.ts:176 `basedOnSeq: input.basedOnSeq ?? 0`, which under the new EQUALITY gate is now strictly worse than before — it fabricates a value that is guaranteed to be refused STALE_BASE against any horizon past seq 0, so the adapter must omit the field instead; eapInitiate outside serialTransaction; the structuredClone / roundtrip-index cost in persistent-delta.ts; MAX_RECALL_BATCHES exhaustion signalling (tools/eap.ts:827 breaks out of the loop and reports whatever partial progress exists, with no distinct refusal); and capability execution / persistent-delta admission still having no cognitive.* tool, reachable only via startServer().eap(tenantId) — which is where the LOW AUTH_BYPASS scope observation above lives.

cognitive.recall accepts and validates a `checkpoint` argument (tools/eap.ts:738) that is then never used — resumption is driven entirely by the durable checkpoint. Passing checkpoint:999999 returned a normal completed recall. Harmless today, but an argument that is validated and discarded invites a client to believe it is resuming from a point it named.

basedOnSeq accepts -0 (Number.isSafeInteger(-0) is true and -0 !== 0 is false), so cognitive.propose with basedOnSeq:-0 against horizon seq 0 is admitted. Cosmetic; recorded only so it is not rediscovered as a finding.
